knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says not to touch unknown substances or enter restricted areas to investigate, to keep bystanders away, and to notify the site contact.
Where a control is missing, the lesson says to isolate the area or postpone the task and notify the site contact. Improvised controls are not used.
The recognise hazards section says to walk the intended work route before unloading.

practicalCriteria: Identifies relevant hazards, scope and site conditions
Selects and explains suitable controls and methods
Performs the sequence without unsafe contamination transfer
Verifies the outcome and documents exceptions
Escalates situations outside training or authority
passRule: Assessor must observe every safety-critical criterion; any failure requires remediation and reassessment.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Look for wet floors, trip hazards, damaged cords, poor lighting, unsecured animals, blocked exits, sharps and signs of hazardous substances.
Record of procedure step 3: Check the site induction information, warning signs, task instructions and any changes since the last visit.
Record of procedure step 5: Keep bystanders away from a suspected hazard.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Look for wet floors, trip hazards, damaged cords, poor lighting, unsecured animals, blocked exits, sharps and signs of hazardous substances.
Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Do not touch unknown substances or enter restricted areas to investigate.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Keep bystanders away from a suspected hazard.
